metadata.title: Salt Lake City dbt companies and people for the Salt Lake City dbt Meetup (no local event yet)
metadata.purpose: Find Salt Lake City companies using dbt, and people who could speak at, co-organise or host a first local Salt Lake City dbt Meetup.
metadata.region: Salt Lake City (Salt Lake City dbt Meetup, no local event yet)
method: v1 (2026-10-05): three parallel runs of about 30 web calls each: dbt job ads and Utah tech employers; other Utah data meetups via meetup gql2 and the Utah Snowflake User Group; company blogs, case studies and women-in-data communities. every link was checked before assembling.
builtin.com Salt Lake City analytics and data-engineering listing pages worked with one fetch each and show a dbt skill tag, but most roles are remote.
Investor job-board mirrors (dcvc, accel, spectrumequity) kept closed ads readable with the data stack.
No named analytics engineer at a Utah employer turned up from ads. Named people came from dbt Labs speaker pages and a dbt community spotlight.
Several fetches returned nothing (builtin single-job pages, Greenhouse boards, amvetsjobs, jointaro). Search summaries were the only evidence for Weave, Health Catalyst and Domo.
Meetup gql2 groupSearch with latitude and longitude plus past events gave the whole local data calendar in one pass, but event text rarely names the speaker.
Search results often answered with unrelated dbt Summit pages; searching a named person worked better than searching a topic.
Utah Data Engineering Meetup is the main local pool; Joe Reis and dbt Labs already ran a dbt event there in 2023.
Search for Utah dbt case studies and engineering blogs returned almost nothing: no Utah company has a dbt Labs, Snowflake or Fivetran case study that the search surfaced.
The Snowflake user group pages (usergroups.snowflake.com/utah) name the local organisers and list host companies for each event, which is the best route to local venues.
dbt Summit speaker pages sometimes state where the speaker lives, which is the only location evidence found for dbt people here.
Built In 'Salt Lake City' job listings are mostly remote roles at companies headquartered elsewhere, so they do not show a local employer.
Job-board pages on careerbuilder.com and edtech.com answer 403 to fetches, and dejobs.org links redirect once an ad has expired.

v2 (2026-10-05): second people pass: about 30 web calls, one at a time, for people not yet on file (first-time speakers, speakers at other local events, women-in-data communities, connectors); every link checked before merging.
Lesson: Utah Data Engineering Meetup event pages (July and Aug 2026) name hosts but not the speaker, so they give no new people.
Lesson: Utah Snowflake User Group event pages list speakers with title and company, and gave the Crumbl speaker.
Lesson: Snowflake Data for Breakfast Salt Lake City (March 2026) lists named local customer speakers.
Lesson: searches for Utah dbt bloggers, newsletters and open source authors returned only job ads and out-of-region authors.

v3 (2026-10-05): third people pass without web search: speaker records of every Utah Snowflake User Group event (bevy data), the meetup speakerDetails field for every 2023-2026 event of the Utah Data Engineering Meetup, Big Data Utah, the Fabric group and SLC Python, and a github user search by Utah location; then one linkedin search per speaker for employer and location.
Lesson: meetup gql2 has a speakerDetails field (name, linkedin) that the event text leaves out; the Utah Data Engineering Meetup names no speaker in its text but fills that field for most events.

Lesson: github user search with location:Utah plus a role word (dbt, analytics engineer, data engineer) finds local practitioners with a stated city, which counts as high-confidence location. Drop accounts with the bio "Data engineer by day, homelab tinkerer by night": they are generated.
Lesson: none of the 178 dbt Summit speaker pages mentions Utah.

v4 (2026-10-05): fourth people pass with research/find_local_speakers.py: 17 local meetup groups (speakerDetails and hosts), the Utah Snowflake and Lehi Tableau chapters, and github users in 22 Wasatch Front towns; then one linkedin lookup per speaker or organiser.
Lesson: MLOps and AI Utah, the Utah SQL Server Group, Salt Lake PyLadies and the Lehi Tableau User Group were not found by search; groupSearch near Salt Lake City lists them.
v5 (2026-10-06): github pass with the faster find_local_speakers.py: data people with a town in the region.

field_definitions.metadata.region: the meetup chapter this dataset serves
field_definitions.metadata.schema_version: shared schema version used by every <region>_dbt_companies.json file (see research/README.md §4)
field_definitions.companies.type: employer | consultancy | vendor | outsourcing | recruiter | community | independent | other
field_definitions.companies.watchlist: true for companies checked but not yet showing in-region dbt work (unconfirmed local presence, or weak/none dbt signal); kept so they are not re-researched
field_definitions.companies.excluded_from_outreach: true for companies deliberately not approached (e.g. dbt Labs staff who already speak regularly)
field_definitions.companies.local_presence: confirmed | not_confirmed | none — whether the company has people/roles in the region
field_definitions.companies.dbt_signal: strong = public post/case study/talk, or dbt required / core stack in a job ad; medium = dbt listed among alternatives, tagged by a job board's skill extraction, or seen only in a snippet; nice-to-have = listed as a plus; weak = unverified; none = stack appears to be non-dbt, or not applicable
field_definitions.companies.other_evidence.type: article | talk | case_study | oss | job_posting | careers | company_blog | conference_talk | meetup | podcast | news | profile | blog_scanned (blog checked, even if nothing relevant) | other
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.dbt_mentioned_in_: true = dbt seen in the ad text (or tagged from the text by the job board); null = only seen in a search snippet about the ad
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.posted_date: date shown on the job board (YYYY-MM-DD), null if unknown
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.last_seen: last run in which the ad was still listed
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.job_family / work: as labelled by the job board (e.g. Analytics Engineer; Remote/Hybrid/On-site); null if not labelled
field_definitions.companies.people.id: kebab-case ASCII name, stable across runs
field_definitions.companies.people.city / based_in_region: city as seen publicly; based_in_region true = evidence they are in the region, false = evidence elsewhere, null = unverified
field_definitions.companies.people.level: leadership if the title contains Head/Director/VP/Chief/Founder/C-level/Manager/Lead, otherwise working
field_definitions.companies.people.confidence: High = name + title + company visible in a public source; Medium = indirect evidence; Low = weak evidence
field_definitions.companies.people.linkedin_confidence: high = name + company/role in the search result title; medium = indirect or name variant; low = searched, not found; not_searched
field_definitions.companies.people.profile_urls: other public professional profiles, as [{type, url, source}]; meetup, x and bluesky profiles can take a message, the others show the person's work: type is one of github, meetup, zenn, qiita, velog, medium, devto, substack, ithome, sessionize, x, bluesky, website, note; source is the page that ties the profile to the person. never an email address or phone number
field_definitions.companies.people.mentions_dbt: true if any of the person's public content (or profile snippet) mentions dbt; false if content found without dbt; null if unknown
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.speaker_pote: high = has given a dbt talk, 2+ public talks, spoke at this chapter before, or priority_tier 1; medium = some public content; low = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.attendee_pot: high = in region and public dbt content (or confirmed practitioner at a strong-dbt company); medium = in-region/unknown data practitioner; low = outside the region or weak identification
field_definitions.companies.people.internal_vinted: true for Vinted colleagues (kept for completeness, not outreach targets)
field_definitions.companies.people.priority_tier: 1 = strong recent lead: a proven speaker with a relevant recent talk, or an emerging_voice in (or not known to be outside) the region with authored content from 2024 onwards; 2 = good lead / needs verification / older content / relevant talk at another meetup; 3 = peripheral, off-topic or remote; organiser / backup / connector = special roles
field_definitions.companies.people.past_chapter_talks: talks this person gave at this chapter's own meetups, matched by name
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.type: talk | panel | podcast | article | case_study | oss | interview | organiser | host | post | profile
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.conten: stable id; an item with several authors appears under each of them with the same content_id
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.url_pr: direct = the item itself; overview_page = a listing/homepage where the item appears
field_definitions.past_meetups.talks.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.lead_type: proven_speaker = has given a talk, panel or podcast, or spoke at this chapter; emerging_voice = has authored public content (blog post, article, newsletter, open-source project, LinkedIn post) but no talk found yet — a priority for first-time speaker invitations; featured = only quoted or profiled in someone else's content (case study, interview, team feature); no_public_content = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.pronouns: pronouns exactly as the person publishes them (e.g. on a speaker listing, bio or profile headline); null when not self-stated. Never inferred from names, photos or third-person wording
field_definitions.companies.people.sourced_via: channels through which the person was found (list): company_blog_scan | case_study | conference_or_meetup_agenda | data_berlin_meetup | women_in_data_community | chapter_meetup_history | newsletter_or_blog | podcast | github | linkedin_search | job_ad_company_search | other

caveats: Ads on investor mirrors are closed, so they show the stack, not open roles.
Board dbt tags come from automatic extraction. Remote roles do not show a Utah office.
Brandon Thomson and Safiyy Momen details come from search summaries; their pages did not load fully. Verify before outreach.
Only about 20 web calls were used; Qualtrics, Pluralsight, Vivint, Entrata, Ancestry, Beyond, Purple, CHG, Nav, BILL, Goldman and Adobe were not confirmed either way.
Titles, employers and cities come from search snippets and meetup pages; verify before outreach.
Many meetup talks have no named speaker in the event text, so only named speakers are listed.
Ternary Data, Buster and Weave details are from search snippets only.
Salt Lake City meetup venues and Big Mountain Data & Dev 2026 speakers were not found.
Titles, employers and cities come from public pages and search snippets; verify before outreach.
The Utah Snowflake user group kickoff page shows 14 April 2025 but calls it a Tuesday; 14 April is a Tuesday in 2026, so the year is uncertain.

No women-in-data community with a Salt Lake City chapter was confirmed: no WiDS Utah, R-Ladies Salt Lake City or Women in Data Utah event surfaced, and the Women Tech Council results were general tech events.
Employers of Noah Goodrich, Chandu Yaramasu and Daniel O'Hare were not found.
Titles, employers and cities come from public pages and snippets; verify before outreach.
No first-time speaker with a verified Utah location was found.
Noah Goodrich (already on file) is listed as Staff Data Engineer at LimbleCMMS on the August 2025 Crumbl event page; his employer on file may need updating.
Dean Raynes and Mason Lancaster are located by employer office (CHG Healthcare, Midvale) plus a local in-person event, so location is medium evidence.
